text:
alex: quick heads-up — ran a latency sweep for TP all-reduce on 8xA100-80GB, message sizes 256B up to 4MB. hitting a sharp latency cliff around ~8KB when the kernel selector switches to ring. tree is faster there. attaching short findings.

alex: summary (p50 wall):
- 256B: ring 0.42ms, tree 0.60ms
- 2KB: ring 0.58ms, tree 0.65ms
- 8KB: ring 3.1ms, tree 1.05ms  <-- big gap
- 32KB: ring 1.2ms, tree 1.3ms

alex: reproduction command I used:
```bash
./tools/run_collective --topo tp --gpus 8 --msg-size 8192 --mode allreduce --profile nsight --kernel-autoswitch=on
```

alex: short nsight snippet (relevant timeline):
```
NCCL_SEND_RING    [ 0.0ms - 2.8ms ]  // long stalled wait on handshake
KERNEL_ALLREDUCE  [ 0.4ms - 1.0ms ]  // compute shorter but blocked by comm handshake
KV_CACHE_LOOKUP   [ 0.01ms - 0.02ms ] // frequent small lookups from prefix caching
```

maria: hmm — is the selector using message bytes or payload after coalescing? can kvcache/be batching be shrinking the effective msg size so the heuristics misclassify? :thinking:

alex: good q. I forced no-kvcache and reran — cliff persists, but moves slightly (from 8KB to ~10KB). looks like kvcache changes distribution but not root cause.

ryan: do we have a recent kernel-autoswitch change? iirc we changed ring/tree threshold in commit 4b9f.. to favor ring for mid sizes to reduce fanout overhead. could be regression on handshake path for small-ish multi-hop rings.

perf-bot: perf-regression-detect v3.2 — regression signal detected in /canary/tp-allreduce between builds 2026-03-01 -> 2026-03-07. metric: p50-latency increased by 2.3x at ~8KB. Suspect: kernel-selector delta 4b9f->6c2e.

katie: i also noticed increased small-message contention in traces when we have heavy prefix caching. many small reductions are scheduled back-to-back causing nccl rendezvous to re-negotiate, amplifying handshake. possible mitigation: keep-alive / sticky coll contexts to reuse MVAPICH-like handshakes or prefer tree for multi-hop.

alex: tried env override to force tree: 
```bash
export REDWOOD_KERNEL_PREF=tree
./tools/run_collective --msg-size 8192 ...
```
result: p50 dropped from 3.1ms -> 1.02ms. bandwidth similar. so tree path avoids handshake blow-up in our topo.

ryan: can you dump NCCL debug trace with NCCL_DEBUG=TRACE? want to see rendezvous messages and whether algorithms oscillate across steps.

alex: pasted trimmed trace excerpt:
```
[0] ncclCommInitRank handshake start
[0] coll_op allreduce msg=8192 algo=RING peer0->peer7 handshake-wait 2387us
[3] coll_op allreduce msg=8192 algo=RING peer3->peer4 handshake-wait 2401us
```
shows lots of handshake waits ~2.3ms.

maria: that aligns with a race where ring builds per-chunk channels and stalls while other peers arrive. tree builds a single aggregation tree and avoids repeated per-chunk negotiation.

katie: next steps suggestion: 1) add a quick feature flag to kernel selector to bias toward tree for msg sizes in 4K-32K on TP topologies that are >4 hops. 2) add metric to console: "allreduce-handshake-wait" p50/p95. 3) run A/B with/without kvcache to quantify interaction.

infra-ci: FYI the canary where kernel-autoswitch landed (build 2026-03-05) is still marked as deployed to staging. i can spin an isolated canary with the tree-bias flag if you want.

ryan: +1 to tree-bias flag. we should also instrument kernel-selector with the effective coalesced msg-size (post-kvcache/batching) — right now it uses declared msg-size which diverges.

alex: created ticket RED-4523 with the trace and numbers, assigned to eng-runtime. i'll add a reproducer script and the nsight capture. planning quick canary tomorrow.

maria: if you need a quick perf test harness, i can adapt the mini-bench into docker-run that toggles kvcache/batching and records handshake microseconds.

alex: that would be great, thanks. tagging @ryan for selector change review and @infra-ci to run canary. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: note — adding regression alert when handshake-wait p95 > 1ms for 3 consecutive canary runs.

katie: also add a note in release notes: "TP all-reduce: temporary tree preference for mid-size messages to avoid handshake regressions (opt-in flag)" so customers can opt-in if they see issues.

alex: thanks all — i'll post canary link and summary when ready.

infra-ci: canary queued (id: canary-2026-03-12-87). will report after 6 runs.
